subject.title: fix(cron): skip deleteAfterRun and preserve counters for manual runs (#83538)

question: Should OpenClaw define manual `cron run` as a non-consuming verification path that records the last outcome but does not mutate scheduled delete/retry/backoff/alert state, including exposing `lastRunWasManual` in cron state?
rationale: The implementation is coherent, but the durable product contract determines whether manual runs should be allowed to consume one-shot jobs or participate in scheduled retry and alert state.

options.title: Accept Non-Consuming Manual Runs
options.body: Merge this direction with explicit maintainer sign-off that manual cron runs are verification-only and scheduled state advances only from scheduler-owned runs.

options.title: Limit To DeleteAfterRun Only
options.body: Ask the author to preserve one-shot jobs while retaining selected manual counter, backoff, or alert side effects if maintainers want manual runs to behave more like real executions.

options.title: Keep Consuming Manual Semantics
options.body: Close or rework the PR and require users to avoid or explicitly override destructive manual runs, leaving the linked issue's preferred behavior unresolved.

recommendation.title: Accept Non-Consuming Manual Runs
recommendation.body: Merge this direction with explicit maintainer sign-off that manual cron runs are verification-only and scheduled state advances only from scheduler-owned runs.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest sampled history across cron runtime and manual-run behavior and is the best available owner for the product-contract decision.
